lesson: Today, we work on one technique, holding time still. That means the poem stops the clock and keeps you in a single moment instead of moving forward. Look at how it stalls. The apple is caught between what it was and what it means to be. The person sits half risen, half in dream. The whole thing rests in the good long pause before a thing gets started. Nothing finishes. Everything is part way. This works in a simple way. When the poem refuses to move ahead, you wait with it. The waiting builds up. Then, so, up, breaks the pause and the sudden motion feels like a release because you held still so long. Try this. Describe one moment right before something happens and use half finished states to keep it from ending. The second time through, feel how long the poem makes you wait. So, so, up, hits harder when it comes.
